'''Aleksej Pokuševski''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Алексеј Покушевски}}, {{lang-gr|Αλεξέι Ποκουσέβσκι}}; born December 26, 2001) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]] of the [[EuroLeague]], and formerly of the [[Olympiacos B.C. B|club's reserve team]]. 

Pokuševski shone as a youth player for the Greek club, [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Pireaus]]. He debuted for their senior team in 2019, at age 17, becoming the youngest [[EuroLeague]] player in club history.

In addition to being a citizen of Serbia, Pokuševski also has Greek citizenship.<ref name="nbacom"/>

== Early career ==
Pokuševski grew up in [[Novi Sad]], where he started to play youth basketball for local clubs, KK Kadet, KK NS Stars, and [[KK Vojvodina|Vojvodina]]. In 2015, Pokuševski joined the [[youth system]] of [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]]. In 2017, he participated in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] camp. In August 2018, he participated at the [[Basketball Without Borders]] Europe camp, in [[Belgrade]], Serbia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jokic, Vucevic Headline Basketball Without Borders Europe 2018 |url=http://global.nba.com/news/jokic-vucevic-headline-basketball-without-borders-europe-2018/ |website=global.nba.com |accessdate=20 March 2019}}</ref> In February 2019, Pokuševski participated at the [[NBA All-Star]] Basketball Without Borders Global Camp, in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 NBA All-Stars Nikola Jokić and Nikola Vučević, Deandre Ayton and Bogdan Bogdanović to coach top international prospects at fifth annual Basketball Without Borders Camp |url=https://pr.nba.com/bwb-global-camp-2019-all-star/ |website=pr.nba.com |accessdate=20 March 2019}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
On March 19, 2019, Pokuševski made his [[EuroLeague]] debut with [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos Piraeus]], in a 89–69 win over the German club [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]], during the EuroLeague's [[2018–19 EuroLeague|2018–19 season]]. He recorded 1 point, 2 rebounds and 1 assist, in one minute played during the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2018-19 Regular Season Round 27 Olympiacos Piraeus 89 - 69 FC Bayern Munich |url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=211&seasoncode=E2018#!boxscore |website=euroleague.net |accessdate=20 March 2019}}</ref> Pokuševski became the youngest senior men's Olympiacos player to ever debut in the EuroLeague. At 17 years and 83 days old, he replaced [[Georgios Printezis]], who had previously debuted in the EuroLeague, at the age of 17 years and 229 days, as the club's youngest ever EuroLeague player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aleksej Pokusevski became youngest ever Olympiacos player to debut in EuroLeague |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/847137/aleksej-pokusevski-became-youngest-ever-olympiacos-player-to-debut-in-euroleague/ |website=eurohoops.net |accessdate=20 March 2019}}</ref>

For the [[2019–20 Greek A2 Basket League|2019–20 season]], Pokuševski was assigned to play in the [[Greek A2 Basket League|Greek A2 League]], the country's second-tier league, with Olympiacos' [[reserve team]], [[Olympiacos BC B Development Team|Olympiacos B]]. He initially played for the senior EuroLeague club's [[practice squad]]. During the season, Pokuševski missed almost 3 months of playing time, due to a [[knee injury]].<ref>[https://stats.nba.com/articles/2020-nba-draft-profile-Aleksej-Pokusevski/ 2020 NBA Draft Profile: Aleksej Pokusevski.]</ref><ref>[https://advanceprobasketball.com/2020/05/06/aleksej-pokusevski-scouting-report-by-zachary-smith/ Aleksej Pokusevski Injury History.]</ref>

Pokuševski started in eight of his 11 appearances in the Greek A2, averaging 10.8 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.8 blocks in 23.1 minutes per game. He shot 40.4 percent from the field, 32.1 percent from 3-point range, and 78.3 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Aleksej-Pokusevski/Summary/130811  International Regular Season Stats - Per Game.]</ref> In the middle of the season, Olympiacos' main EuroLeague team was riddled with injuries, and Pokuševski was called up to the senior team. He played two minutes in his only EuroLeague game of the season,<ref>[https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=008232&seasoncode=E2019 POKUSEVSKI, ALEKSEJ OLYMPIACOS PIRAEUS EuroLeague 2019-20 STATISTICS.]</ref> before the league's season was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]. Pokuševski earned Greek A2 [[Bosman ruling|Bosman eligible]] Player of the Year and All-Defensive Team honors from the website [[Eurobasket.com]], which should be noted, are not awards given by the league and are unofficial.<ref name="mammides">{{cite web |last1=Mammides |first1=Chris |title=Eurobasket.com All-Greek A2 Awards 2020 |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/626133/Eurobasket |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=April 17, 2020}}</ref>

On April 24, 2020, Pokuševski declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Giviony |first1=Jonathan |title=Serbian forward Aleksej Pokusevski declares for NBA draft
|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/story/_/id/29094835/serbian-forward-aleksej-pokusevski-declares-nba-draft|website=espn.com |accessdate=24 April 2020}}</ref> Pokuševski's [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]] contract lasts through the end of the 2023–24 season. The contract's [[buyout clause]] for the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] is €1 million euros, if he is a top 20 [[NBA draft|draft]] pick, or €1.5 million euros, if he is a top 14 [[lottery pick]].<ref>[https://www.novasports.gr/the-experts/article/1761085/o-%E2%80%98%E2%80%99pokou%E2%80%99%E2%80%99-fernei-zesto-xrima-sto-tameio-tou-olumpiakou O ‘’Ποκού’’ φέρνει ζεστό χρήμα στο ταμείο του Ολυμπιακού! {{in lang|it}}.]</ref><ref>[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1053853/aleksej-pokusevskis-nba-buyout-may-reportedly-near-1-5m/ Aleksej Pokusevski’s NBA buyout may reportedly near 1.5M.]</ref>

== National team career ==
Pokuševski was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-17 basketball team|Serbian national under-17 team]] that competed at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], in [[Argentina]]. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 7.7 points, 8.3 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 3.0 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aleksej POKUSEVSKI at the 2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Aleksej-Pokusevski |website=fiba.basketball |accessdate=20 March 2019}}</ref>

Pokuševski was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-18 basketball team|Serbian national under-18 team]] that competed at the [[2019 FIBA Under-18 European Championship]], in [[Volos]], Greece. Over seven tournament games, he averaged 10.0 points, 7.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.7 steals, and 4.0 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 Serbia U18 - Pokusevski |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2019/player/Aleksej-Pokusevski |website=fiba.basketball |accessdate=8 August 2019}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Pokuševski's family originates from [[Priština]], [[Kosovo]]. Due to the [[Kosovo War]] in 1999, his family escaped to [[Podgorica]] (nowadays in [[Montenegro]]), and moved to [[Belgrade]], [[Serbia]], afterwards, where Pokuševski was born in 2001. Thereafter, Pokuševski and his family permanently moved to [[Novi Sad]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Zapamtite ovo ime – Aleksej Pokuševski VIDEO |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2019&mm=03&dd=19&nav_id=1519967 |website=b92.net |accessdate=20 March 2019|language=sr}}</ref> 

After signing a youth team contract with the Greek basketball club [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]], Pokuševski moved to [[Greece]] in 2015, at the age of 13. While playing in Greek competitions, he counts as a native Greek domestic player, since he started competing in Greek competitions before the age of 14.<ref>[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/trademarks/994454/the-progress-card-of-10-european-nba-draft-prospects/11/ The progress card of 10 European NBA draft prospects.]</ref> He was eligible to represent either Serbia or [[Greece]] in [[national sports team|national team]] competitions, and he chose to represent Serbia.<ref name="nbacom"/>
